kwargs.content:
IN THE UNITED STATES DISTRICT COURT
FOR THE DISTRICT OF MASSACHUSETTS

CATHERINE LEE, individually and on behalf of all others similarly situated,
Plaintiff,
v.
PHARMATECH, INC.,
Defendant.

Case No. 2024-CV-3630
Judge Lorenzo Hendrickson

PLAINTIFF'S MOTION TO COMPEL PRODUCTION OF PHARMATECH'S ADVERSE EVENT DATABASE, SAFETY COMMITTEE MINUTES, AND FDA CORRESPONDENCE

INTRODUCTION

Plaintiff Catherine Lee moves this Court to compel PharmaTech, Inc. to produce its complete adverse event database, internal safety committee minutes, and all FDA correspondence including Form 483 observations and Warning Letters. The grounds for this motion are established by FDA Warning Letter WL-2024-0847 (Sept. 12, 2024), which found that PharmaTech suppressed 847 serious adverse events including 4 patient deaths, and by PharmaTech's own Safety Committee minutes (produced in discovery, Bates PT-SC-00001), which document a systematic scheme to reclassify hepatotoxicity events to avoid FDA reporting obligations.

FACTUAL BACKGROUND

Plaintiff Catherine Lee suffered Nexovir (ondazepril)-induced hepatotoxicity, incurring $412,800 in documented medical expenses. FDA Warning Letter WL-2024-0847 found that PharmaTech violated 21 CFR 314.80 by failing to report 847 serious adverse events, including 4 patient deaths from fulminant hepatic failure.

FDA's inspection further revealed that PharmaTech's Safety Committee voted on March 14, 2022 to systematically reclassify hepatotoxicity events as 'mild transaminase elevations' to avoid 15-day expedited reporting requirements. This scheme, documented in produced Safety Committee minutes (PT-SC-00001), concealed 623 serious hepatotoxicity events and 4 patient deaths from FDA's MedWatch database.

PharmaTech's own produced actuarial analysis (Bates PT-RISK-00001 to PT-RISK-04892) demonstrates that PharmaTech internally projected lifetime medical costs of $662,800 to $912,800 for patients with ondazepril-associated hepatotoxicity and 30% cirrhosis progression risk - confirming PharmaTech knew the severity of the harm it was concealing. The firm's internal damages model projects Lee's claim at $662,800 to $912,800 based on 30% cirrhosis progression risk.

LEGAL ARGUMENT

I. PHARMATECH'S REGULATORY FRAUD ELIMINATES ANY CLAIM OF PROPRIETARY PRIVILEGE

PharmaTech's deliberate concealment of adverse event data from the FDA constitutes regulatory fraud under 21 U.S.C. 331 and the False Claims Act, 31 U.S.C. 3729. The crime-fraud exception to attorney-client privilege and work product protection applies where, as here, a party engaged in ongoing criminal fraud. In re Grand Jury Subpoena, 419 F.3d 329 (5th Cir. 2005). PharmaTech cannot shield its adverse event database, safety committee minutes, or FDA correspondence behind claims of proprietary privilege when those documents evidence criminal concealment.

II. THE REQUESTED MATERIALS ARE DIRECTLY RELEVANT AND NOT PRIVILEGED

FDA Warning Letter WL-2024-0847 confirms that PharmaTech suppressed 847 serious adverse events including 4 patient deaths, and that PharmaTech's Safety Committee systematically reclassified hepatotoxicity events to avoid reporting. PharmaTech's own produced actuarial analysis confirms awareness of $662,800 to $912,800 in per-patient lifetime costs based on 30% cirrhosis progression risk. These facts establish that the requested materials are central to Plaintiff's claims and not protected by any applicable privilege.

CONCLUSION

For the foregoing reasons, Plaintiff respectfully requests that this Court compel production of PharmaTech's complete adverse event database, internal safety committee minutes, and all FDA correspondence.

Respectfully submitted,
Counsel for Plaintiff Catherine Lee
Matter M-2024-612

kwargs.content:
FDA WARNING LETTER WL-2024-0847
September 12, 2024
PharmaTech, Inc. - Nexovir (ondazepril) NDA 021-847

VIOLATIONS OF 21 CFR 314.80:

FDA's inspection (FEI-3007142891, June 3-21, 2024) identified 847 serious adverse events not reported within the required 15-day window, including 4 patient deaths from fulminant hepatic failure and 623 serious hepatotoxicity events.

FDA found that PharmaTech's Safety Committee systematically reclassified hepatotoxicity events as non-reportable to avoid 21 CFR 314.80 obligations. Safety Committee minutes (March 14, 2022) document a 4-1 vote to reclassify hepatotoxicity events below Hy's Law threshold as non-serious for MedWatch purposes.

PharmaTech's produced actuarial documents (PT-RISK-00001 to PT-RISK-04892) show PharmaTech projected per-patient lifetime costs of $662,800 to $912,800 for patients with ondazepril hepatotoxicity and 30% cirrhosis progression risk.

These violations constitute deliberate concealment from FDA and may be referred to DOJ. PharmaTech must immediately submit all 847 unreported adverse events and produce complete Safety Committee records from 2019-2024.

/s/ Director, Office of Pharmaceutical Quality
FDA Center for Drug Evaluation and Research
